artworks.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
artworks.description: Goya's Saturn devouring his son — the Titan father swallowing his children so none will unseat him.

artworks.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
artworks.description: Rubens' Saturn devouring his son — Baroque horror of the same Theogonic crime that empties Rhea's nursery.

artworks.title: Rhea Presents the Swaddled Stone to Cronus (relief)
artworks.description: Rhea presents the swaddled stone — the trick that saves Zeus while Cronus swallows a rock in place of his youngest.

artworks.title: Rhea Handing the Swaddled Stone to Cronus
artworks.description: The Nausicaä Painter's vase: Rhea hands Cronus the stone — the hinge between the swallowed siblings and Zeus' rise.

popCulture.title: Theogony
popCulture.creator: Hesiod
popCulture.description: Hesiod's Cronus swallows Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, and Poseidon — until the stone and Zeus force the disgorging.

popCulture.title: Cronus
popCulture.description: The Titan who ate his children remains Western myth's image of time devouring its own succession.

popCulture.title: Rhea (mythology)
popCulture.description: The mother who saved Zeus with a swaddled stone — the hinge between swallowed siblings and Olympian rule.
